CITY  OF  ALHAMBRA

  REGULARMEETING OF THE
  ALHAMBRA HOUSING AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT
  CITIZEN ADVISORY COMMITTEE

The Regular Meeting of the Alhambra Housing and Community Development Citizen
Advisory (HCDA) Committee will be held on Tuesday, August 4, 2020, commencing at
7:00 p.m. via teleconference and video conference.

  CORONAVIRUS (COVID-19) ADVISORY NOTICE

Consistent with Executive Orders No. N-29-20 and No. N-35-20 from the Executive
Department of the State of California and the County of Los Angeles Department of Public
Health Safer At Home Order, the Alhambra Housing and Community Development
Citizen Advisory Committee meeting will not be physically open to the public and the
meeting will take place via teleconference and video conference.

To watch and listen to the meeting: To maximize public safety while still maintaining
transparency and public access, members of the public can participate by using Zoom
Meeting as follows:

Zoom direct link:

https://us02web.zoom.us/j/86741594249?pwd=M2RoZDl2dmxnaUJsVC82WURydGVx
dz09

Enter ID: 867 4159 4249 and Passcode: 580473

Or by telephone by dialing: 1-669-900-9128 or 1-346-248-7799 or 1-253-215-8782 or 1-
312-626-6799 or 1-646-558-8656 or 1-301-715-8592

Enter ID: 867 4159 4249 and Passcode: 580473

Please Note: All members of the public calling or logging into the meeting will be muted
so that the meeting can proceed. For those wishing to speak on an agenda item, please
email Matthew Cuevas at mcuevas@cityofalhambra.org by 5:00 p.m. prior to the meeting
with the item number you wish to speak on and the phone number you will use when
calling or the name you will use when logging into the meeting. You should then call or
log into the meeting at least 5 minutes prior to its start time. Staff will unmute you and
announce you when it is your time to speak. You will have five minutes to speak, unless
that time is adjusted by the meeting Chair. Given the challenges of teleconference and
video conference meetings, all participants are encouraged to email their comments
prior to the beginning of the meeting.

Comments can be emailed to the Matthew Cuevas at mcuevas@cityofalhambra.org by no
later than 5:00 p.m. on August 4, 2020 to ensure there is sufficient time to print the emails
prior to the beginning of the meeting. Comments will then be read into the record, with a
 maximum allowance of 5 minutes per individual comment, subject to the Chair’s
discretion. If a comment is received after 5:00 p.m. but before the conclusion of the
meeting based upon its time stamp, the comment will still be included as a part of the
record of the meeting but will not be read into the record.

An agenda of the regular meeting is attached hereto incorporated herein by reference and
made a part hereof as though fully set forth herein.
   AGENDA
  REGULAR MEETING
HOUSING AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT CITIZEN ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  TUESDAY, AUGUST 4, 2020 AT 7:00 P.M.

1. ROLL CALL:
  Bill Vallejos, Chair  Mark Lee, Vice Chair
  Bonita Sharma-Ngan  Andrea Giese
  Marc Tousignant  Sasha Renée Pérez
  Maria Conchita Bañuelos  Yvette Cardenas
  Marcos Sayon

2. MINUTES
  Approval of the minutes for the Special Meeting of June 16, 2020.

3. PROGRESS REPORTS
  Attached for the Committee’s review are copies of the Progress Reports for those programs
  utilizing Community Development Block Grant and HOME Funds. All figures indicate the
  progress made and services rendered to date for FY 2019-2020.
   Parks and Recreation - Case Management
   105 Case Management clients were served.
   135 Volunteer Hours of assistance were donated to the program.
   Community Development - Code Enforcement
   The Code Enforcement Division investigated a total of 576 complaints.
   84 were identified as confirmed complaints as stand-alone Health & Safety Issues.
   Code Enforcement staff referred 553 to the Housing Department programs.
   Community Development - Fair Housing
   The Housing Rights Center served approx. 318 clients.
   A variety of issues were discussed, including: evictions, security deposits, rent
  increases, repairs, contract questions, etc.
   Community Development - Housing Programs
   First-Time Home Buyer - HOME: 9 searching for a home, 2 escrow closed.
   HOME Major Rehabilitation: 0 in process, 1 completed.
   CDBG Minor Rehabilitation: 0 in process, 1 completed.

  Recommended Action
  Receive and file these informational reports.

4. PRESENTATIONS FROM HOUSING RIGHTS CENTER AND CODE
  ENFORCEMENT
  The Housing and Community Development Citizens Advisory Committee will hear
  presentations from City Code Enforcement and the Housing Rights Center on their roles and
  responsibilities regarding CDBG funded activities.

  Recommended Action
  Receive and file informational presentations.
 5. COMMENTS FROM THE AUDIENCE
  Discussion from the public of any item not specified on the agenda. Comments must pertain
  to the business of the HCDA Citizen Advisory Committee. Public comments pertaining to
  the HCDA Committee’s business are welcome. Kindly limit all oral communications to five
  (5) minutes. Please complete the blue speaker card prior to the meeting and submit it to the
  Committee’s secretary.

6. COMMENTS AND CONCERNS FROM THE COMMITTEE
  Discussion from the Committee Members of any item(s) not specified on the agenda. Items
  discussed must pertain to the business of the HCDA Citizen Advisory Committee.

7. ADJOURNMENT

 Copies of the staff report or other written documentation relating to each item of business described herein
 above are on file in the office of Management Services, Alhambra City Hall, 111 S. First Street, Alhambra,
 CA, and are available for public inspection during regular office hours: 7:00 A.M. to 5:30 P.M., Monday
 through Thursday.
 Should any person have a question concerning any of the above agenda items prior to the meeting described
 herein, he or she may contact Mr. Matthew Cuevas, Management Analyst, either in person, at the
 Management Services Department located at City Hall, or call via telephone at (626) 570-5011, during
 regular business hours.

 Americans with Disabilities Act: If you require special assistance to participate in any City meeting, please
 contact the City Clerk's Office (626) 570-5090. Notification of at least 72 hours prior to the meeting will
 enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting.
   UNOFFICIAL
  Minutes of the City of Alhambra’s
  HCDA Citizen Advisory Committee
  Special Meeting of June 16, 2020
  MEETING CONDUCTED VIA TELECONFERENCE/ZOOM DUE TO COVID-19.

  Assistant City Manager Garcia called the meeting to order at 7:03 p.m.

1. ROLL CALL:
  Committee Members Present:
  Bill Vallejos, Chair*  Mark Lee, Vice Chair
  Maria Conchita Bañuelos  Andrea Giese
  Marc Tousignant  Bonita Sharma-Ngan
  Sasha Renée Pérez  Yvette Cardenas

  *Committee Chair Vallejos joined the meeting at 7:22 p.m.

  Committee Members Absent:
  Marcos Sayon

  City Staff Present:
  Lucy Garcia, Assistant City Manager
  Veronica Tam, Veronica Tam and Associates
  Matthew Cuevas, Management Analyst

  New HCDA Committee Member, Yvette Cardenas, was introduced by Assistant City
  Manager Garcia.

2. MINUTES
  The Committee reviewed the minutes for the Special Meeting of January 30, 2020.

  Committee Action:
  Vice Chair Lee moved, seconded by Committee Member Bañuelos, to approve the minutes
  for the special meeting of January 30, 2020.
  Ayes:  Lee, Sharma-Ngan, Bañuelos, Giese, Tousignant, Pérez and Cardenas.
  Noes:  None.
  Abstain: None.

3. PROGRESS REPORTS
  The Committee reviewed the reports. All figures indicate the progress made and services
  rendered to date for FY 2019-2020. Assistant City Manager Garcia gave an overview of the
  current progress reports, including the additional COVID-19 funding under CDBG for
  COVID-19 testing and for a housing assistance program for 200 low- and moderate-income
  households to provide $500 a month for rental/mortgage assistance payments for three
  months.

  Committee Member Pérez inquired how many applications were received for the housing
  assistance program, how applicants were notified, and any households that may have include
  undocumented individuals.

  Page 1 of 4
   Assistant City Manager Garcia answered the City received approximately 2,000 applications,
  and City staff has been processing applications as quickly as possible. Assistant City
  Manager Garcia added that approximately 70 to 75 applicants had been approved to date. In
  addition, applicants also need to provide proper identification, income status, and permanent
  resident or citizenship, per HUD requirements, to be eligible for funding.

  Committee Member Cardenas asked about the COVID-19 testing aspect moving from
  symptomatic individuals only to including asymptomatic individuals, and other uses the
  CDBG funds could be used for such as assistance for small businesses.

  Assistant City Manager Garcia replied the City tested 1,599 individuals and ultimately
  included asymptomatic individuals due to the health department encouraging the testing of
  these individuals since they could still spread the virus. Assistant City Manager also replied
  the City received a list from HUD for eligible COVID related activities and it left each
  jurisdiction discretion on how to apply those funds and those were the concepts that City
  Council approved.

  Committee Member Pérez asked if the City was going to be receiving any additional CDBG
  funds.

  Assistant City Manager Garcia replied at this time the City does not anticipate any additional
  CDBG funding but ultimately it would be up to Congress and the President.

  Committee Action:
  The Committee received and filed these informational reports.

4. DRAFT 2020-2024 CONSOLIDATED PLAN AND 2020-2021 ANNUAL ACTION
  PLAN
  Assistant City Manager Garcia introduced Veronica Tam to provide the presentation on the
  draft 2020-2024 Consolidated Plan and the 2020-2021 Annual Action Plan.

  Ms. Tam opened her presentation by sharing the list of eligible activities, provided by HUD,
  regarding the CDBG COVID-19 funding to the Committee, and outlined some of the
  challenges of setting up these activities without violating HUD policies. One challenge was
  ensuring that jurisdictions were not providing a duplication of benefits under HUD policies.

  Assistant City Manager Garcia spoke about the business assistance aspect and at the time
  many programs were being offered through the state and the county, the City wanted to
  ensure there wasn’t a duplication of benefits.

  Ms. Tam began her presentation on the 2020-2024 Consolidated Plan and 2020-2021 Annual
  Action Plan. She informed the Committee that the City has received over $1 million in
  federal funding. Ms. Tam also reiterated that the HOME funds are used for increasing and
  preserving affordable housing for low- and moderate-income households and cannot be used
  in any other way. Ms. Tam also noted that this is the first time over her entire career where
  the designation for an Urgent Need under HUD has been authorized due to COVID-19.

  Ms. Tam touched upon the revised goals and priorities the Committee agreed upon as a result
  of prior HCDA meetings including:

  − Conserve and improve existing affordable housing
  Page 2 of 4
   − Support housing Code Enforcement Services
  − Support affordable housing opportunities
  − Promote equal housing opportunity
  − Provide needed community and supportive services, especially for Senior Services
  − Provide community facility/infrastructure improvement, especially ADA projects
  − Provide for planning and administrative activities

In her presentation Ms. Tam discussed the upcoming 2020-2021 CDBG Action Plan and
reviewed the Committee’s revised funding priorities including:

  −  $314,374 for Housing Rehabilitation
  −  $344,798 for Code Enforcement
  −  $25,000 for Fair Housing Services
  −  $152,117 for Senior Case Management Services
  −  $177,822 for Administration

Ms. Tam then reiterated the Committee’s revised funding priorities for the 2020-2021
HOME Action Plan, including:

  − $451,469 for Housing Rehabilitation
  − $146,064 for CHDO Reserve
  − $66,393 for Administration

Assistant City Manager Garcia informed the Committee that since the last meeting, the City
had received a small increase in funding from HUD.

Committee Member Tousignant inquired what the new amount was.

Assistant City Manager Garcia answered it was approximately $100,000 and the additional
funds were spread out among the various priorities the Committee had identified prior.

Committee Member Pérez asked about Code Enforcement activities in relation to affordable
housing issues and citations issued for minor violations like peeling paint or brown lawns.

Assistant City Manger Garcia and Ms. Tam answered that the CDBG portion of Code
Enforcement funding can only be used in the designated target areas throughout the City that
utilize CDBG funds, and any enforcement actions are restricted to major building code and
health and safety violations. Assistant City Manager Garcia stated City staff would arrange
for a future presentation from Code Enforcement to provide the Committee with an overview
of the division’s responsibilities.

Committee Member Cardenas inquired about a table in the draft plan that was not displaying
percentages or proportions and asked if those could be added into the table.

Ms. Tam agreed with Committee Member Cardenas that the tables were challenging but
answered unfortunately the tables could not be updated because the template is provided by
HUD. Ms. Tam further explained that technical documentation on how to present census
data, from the American Community Survey data, should never be presented as absolute
numbers since they are survey estimates.

  Page 3 of 4
   Committee Member Cardenas asked if the unemployment figures in the draft document can
  be updated to reflect the current numbers and noted there was missing information on page
  12 relating to table 11.

  Ms. Tam answered she would check to see if the Bureau of Labor Statistics had published
  updated numbers, and if they are available, she would include those revised figures. In
  addition, she would correct any revisions to table 11.

  Committee Member Cardenas inquired about the removal of the First Time Homebuyer
  program.

  Ms. Tam explained the reasoning why the Committee decided to eliminate that program and
  the difficulty of purchasing a home with a price that meets HUD standards.

  Committee Member Pérez asked if residents would be eligible for Los Angeles County’s
  First Time Homebuyer Program.

  Ms. Tam answered it depended on the funding source and most communities throughout the
  state do not offer this type of program, she noted the state Housing and Community
  Development Department may offer other programs.

  Committee Member Bañuelos added there are non-profit organizations that offer down
  payment assistance and first-time homebuyer programs in Los Angeles County.

  Committee Action:
  Chair Vallejos moved, seconded by Committee Member Bañuelos, to approve the draft 2020-
  2024 Consolidated Plan and 2020-2021 Annual Action Plan and initiate the public comment
  period in anticipation for City Council adoption at the next regularly scheduled City Council
  Meeting.
  Ayes:  Vallejos, Lee, Sharma-Ngan, Bañuelos, Giese, Tousignant, Pérez and Cardenas.
  Noes:  None.
  Abstain: None.

5. COMMENTS FROM THE AUDIENCE
  None.

6. COMMENTS AND CONCERNS FROM THE COMMITTEE
  Committee Member Pérez asked if the meeting minutes of January 30 could be revised to
  remove her name since she had not been officially sworn-in at that time.

  Management Analyst Cuevas responded that the official meeting minutes of January 30
  would be revised to reflect that.

7. ADJOURNMENT: Committee Chair Vallejos adjourned the meeting at 8:10 p.m.

OFFICIAL
  Minutes of the City of Alhambra’s
  HCDA Citizen Advisory Committee
  Regular Meeting of August 4, 2020
  MEETING CONDUCTED VIA TELECONFERENCE/ZOOM DUE TO COVID-19.

  Assistant City Manager Garcia called the meeting to order at 7:05 p.m.

1. ROLL CALL:
  Committee Members Present:
  Maria Conchita Bañuelos  Andrea Giese
  Marc Tousignant  Bonita Sharma-Ngan
  Sasha Renée Pérez  Marcos Sayon
  Yvette Cardenas

  Committee Members Absent:
  Bill Vallejos
  Mark Lee

  City Staff Present:
  Lucy Garcia, Assistant City Manager
  Matthew Cuevas, Management Analyst
  Rafael Perez, Code Enforcement Supervisor
  Chancela Al-Mansour, Executive Director, Housing Rights Center

2. MINUTES
  The Committee reviewed the minutes for the Special Meeting of June 16, 2020. Committee
  Member Cardenas requested a minor change on page 2 of the June 16, 2020 minutes.
  Assistance City Manager Garcia stated that change will be made on the official minutes.

  Committee Action:
  Committee Member Bañuelos moved, seconded by Committee Member Tousignant, to
  approve the minutes for the Special Meeting of June 16, 2020 with the requested change.
  Ayes:  Bañuelos, Giese, Sharma-Ngan, Sayon, Tousignant, Pérez and Cardenas.
  Noes:  None.
  Abstain: None.

3. PROGRESS REPORTS
  The Committee reviewed the reports. All figures indicate the progress made and services
  rendered to date for FY 2019-2020. Assistant City Manager Garcia gave an overview of the
  current progress reports for each program area.

  Committee Member Pérez asked for clarification on how HUD funds are used for Code
  Enforcement regarding extreme issues renters are faced with. She spoke about a recent
  incident where a family contacted her and had no electricity or gas since the 4th of July. She
  stated the family had reached out to both Code Enforcement and the Housing Rights Center
  but was unable to get any assistance. The family’s situation was resolved when the Los
  Angeles County Health Department was contacted and a health violation was issued.

  Executive Director Al-Mansour introduced herself and responded to Committee Member

  Executive Director Al-Mansour began her presentation regarding the Housing Rights Center.
  The presentation provided brief background on the Housing Rights Center and the multitude
  of services that are provided and included an overview of the Fair Housing Act. She then
  discussed the effects COVID-19 has had on eviction moratoriums under the California
  Judicial Council’s emergency rule, and local laws and how each city has its own type of
  moratorium order.

  Executive Director Al-Mansour then talked about how COVID-19 changed the way the
  Housing Rights Center is able to provide its services, but noted it has allowed for more
  specialized trainings on eviction moratoriums, housing discrimination, and seminars on
  mental health and ADA reasonable accommodations during COVID-19. Executive Director
  Al-Mansour added the Housing Rights Center also assists landlords with housing issues. She
  concluded her presentation by sharing the Housing Rights Center’s weekly activities
  schedule and stated they were going to do more virtual services to assist clients.

  Housing Rights Center’s website and if the only hours currently offered were during mid-

Assistant City Manager Garcia introduced Code Enforcement Supervisor Perez.

Code Enforcement Supervisor Perez began his presentation on the role of the Code
Enforcement Division regarding CDBG funding. Code Enforcement Supervisor Perez
provided a general overview of the areas Code Enforcement is responsible for including
things such as landscaping, graffiti, and substandard living conditions. He also spoke about
  Page 3 of 10
 the internal stakeholders the division coordinates regarding other City departments and the
external stakeholders and partnerships with other agencies.

In responding to Committee Member Pérez’s inquiry about the family with no electricity, he
noted the City does not have a rental inspection program and without this tool, the City relies
heavily on the Los Angeles County Health Department to handles those types of inspections.
Code Enforcement Supervisor Perez also spoke about the other county departments the City
coordinates with. He reiterated the partnership with the Housing Rights Center and providing
information to tenants regarding landlord/tenant issues or any other housing rights violations.

Code Enforcement Supervisor Perez then explained that only serious health and safety issues
qualify as violations under CDBG funding. He explained these violations were things such as
peeling paint on the exterior, major structural issues and other hazardous conditions. Code
Enforcement Supervisor Perez provided examples to the Committee, as well as the various
Code violations that do not qualify under CDBG such as landscaping and litter. He stated that
landscaping and litter violations would be ancillary to the health and safety violations. Code
Enforcement Supervisor Perez also reviewed the number of complaints the Code
Enforcement Division received to date, and noted that only 84 were stand alone health and
safety violations that qualified under CDBG.

Committee Member Pérez inquired if the numbers are just reported to the City of Alhambra.
She referred back to the example of the family that contacted the County and asked if that
gets communicated back to the City and if the City tracks that.

Code Enforcement Supervisor Perez responded in this instance it resulted from a fire that
occurred on July 4 and his office was not contacted until July 21. He stated once the division
was notified, Code Enforcement responded and took photos of the unit. Code Enforcement
Supervisor Perez said a notice was not issued at the time since Code Enforcement wanted to
get further assistance from the City’s Fire Prevention and Building Divisions. He stated all
the divisions returned the next day and issued notices of violations. Code Enforcement
Supervisor Perez also mentioned he has stayed in communication with the family since July
21 to follow up. He stated since there is no rental inspection program or City laws in place,
the City cannot provide mandated emergency housing and impose that on a property owner,
and as a result the family was referred to Los Angeles County for further assistance. Code
Enforcement Supervisor Perez further explained that in this instance the referral to the Los
Angeles County Health Department is what triggered the mechanism for the emergency
housing while the owner mitigated the issues. He restated since the City does not have a
rental housing inspection program, Code Enforcement does not have the tools to impose on a
landlord a requirement to house families who have been displaced, in instances such as this,
at a separate location; however, the owner was instructed to work with the tenants to obtain
the necessary assistance.

Code Enforcement Supervisor Perez continued his presentation and provided examples of
violations that qualify under the CDBG program. He noted that stand alone issues such as
landscaping, trash and vehicles parked on front lawns do not qualify as violations under
CDBG, but are considered routine code violations that would fall under the General Fund
source. Code Enforcement Supervisor Perez described the various enforcement methods up
to administrative citations and criminal prosecution, which he noted were rarely used but is
an available tool Code Enforcement has. He reiterated that Code Enforcement always looks
for education and compliance before issuing citations. He then discussed hoarding situations
and stated the division works with outside groups to assist, as well as coordinating with the
  Page 4 of 10
 homeowner or landlord to address the issue, and make referrals to the Los Angeles County
Department of Mental Health if the situation calls for it.

Committee Member Pérez inquired about one of the examples in the presentation of a private
garage and how Code Enforcement would address that since it is private property and the
garage door closes.

Code Enforcement Supervisor Perez responded if the garage door is open, and Code
Enforcement has received compliant, they would investigate. He noted in this instance an
illegal automotive repair shop was being run out of this residential garage. Code Enforcement
Supervisor Perez said there are 33 sections under the City Code that violations can be
addressed, and Code Enforcement will continue to address any issues to mitigate complaints
but stated the only time Code Enforcement would not get involved is a civil matter.

Committee Member Pérez mentioned at last night’s Planning Commission meeting the issue
of certain permitted conditions for developments being set, but then the conditions are
ignored, and asked if Code Enforcement played a role to ensure that any set conditions are
honored.

Code Enforcement Supervisor Perez responded that the development conditions are done
through the Planning Department and entitlement process, and no active enforcement for
entitlements is conducted unless a complaint is received. He stated City planners assign
requirements to check-in and perform inspections, and if they find an issue they will mitigate
it or refer it Code Enforcement for action. Code Enforcement Supervisor Perez explained that
Code Enforcement is not involved in the step by step process for a project regarding
entitlements.

Committee Member Pérez asked what happens if it is discovered that a project is out of
compliance with entitlements.

Code Enforcement Supervisor Perez replied that Code Enforcement can issue an immediate
stop work order and some of the additional tools for enforcement action can lead up to civil
prosecution or fines. He said Code Enforcement will use tools at their disposal for the
enforcement of policy.

Committee Member Pérez stated that Director Castagnola has said it was difficult to check if
developer was out of compliance and is able to get away with it.

Code Enforcement Supervisor Perez replied if a developer is not complying, would need to
look at that during the development process and speak with his Director regarding Code
Enforcement’s role, and see if Code Enforcement can have a better supplement to those
issues. He then continued his presentation discussing the role Code Enforcement plays in
regards to community policing and crime prevention, and coordinating with the Police
Department and the HOME Team to address illegal encampments and provide help to
homeless individuals.
